children.text: It seems like we hit upon the most obvious answer first and then add nuance as we go along, as if we're witnessing the transition from primitive steak engines to ICEs just sped up hundreds of times.

>Presented in our ICML 2025 paper, this architectural improvement allows models to achieve the same quality up to three times faster with a negligible increase in parameters.

>Rather than passing all prior layers forward with equal weight, DCA introduces a lightweight, layer-wise module that decides how to best combine previous embeddings on a per-token basis.

This combined with looped transformers (as showcased with GLM-5.4 from... 4 days ago) could lead to even more efficiency squeezes without substantially increasing the parameter size or altering data blend. It's hard to fathom how merely 3-4 years ago, many in the industry (despite the Chinchilla paper) thought scaling up the parameter count was the largest leverage wrt bettering model performance as compared to other techniques, but we've had such explosion of techniques since then -- CoT, MoE, RLVR, GQA, Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) and whatnot.
Title: Supercharging Transformer Residual Connections

children.text:
Or you give the model the ability to write code that reads The model’s transcript.

I’m not saying the strawberry problem is a big deal. I’m saying that models often have some difficulty perceiving their own input at a low level, and cross-layer attention seems like it could help in general.

the strawberry problem is not a real problem and it's been understood how to solve it since it showed up. nobody does it because its not worth the compute.

besides making the letters visible in some way, you need to remove softmax normalization (not for the full model! just for the sections of it that do the counting) since it only allows you to represent outputs as a fraction of the inputs. no model architecture that normalizes this way will ever truly learn integer counting that generalizes to unseen inputs.

you also need a different activation function, relu and family cut away some crucial information.

just copy paste what I told you into a claude conversation, they can train a small llm that shows it easily on their server cpu or locally on your machine.

> Depth-wise cross-attention (split Q/K/V): While standard transformer attention operates across tokens in a sequence, DCA applies attention across layers in depth. Each token queries a dynamically weighted mix of all prior layer embeddings, unlocking the model's full historical context without the computational penalty usually required to scale traditional attention.

I’ve often thought that something like this might lead to a real solution to the infamous strawberry problem.

Ignoring pesky issues like tokenization, the actual input data is visible to the model as the embedding fed to the first layer, but the first layer is probably nowhere near smart enough to understand that the model is trying to count R instances. But by the time whatever layer is reached that might understand the goal, the non-wasteful part of the low-level memory (the K’s and V’s from the first layer) can’t be queried any more.

But this cross-depth attention can query them!

Admittedly, there are holes in this argument. Beyond just tokenization (to the extent that the model can see letters at all, it is reconstructing them), the attention mechanism doesn’t really have a clean “count the hits” operation.
